subject: english
title: 3-Ⅳ-13：從角色、舞台指示與衝突理解簡易短劇

content.summary: 短劇的意義同時存在於台詞、舞台指示、道具、燈光、走位與結局；不能只讀角色說出的句子。本課以遺失錢包、主持報告、黑窗、末班車、班級禮物、跳電、犯錯後發言、紅圍巾、傾聽與失蹤布條等原創劇本，練習角色目標、舞台動作、衝突、線索、解決方案、象徵、人物改變與結局主旨。

sections.heading: 先分辨台詞和舞台指示
sections.body: 台詞讓觀眾聽見角色的想法或行動，方括號中的 points、steps back、lights go out 則告訴演員如何呈現場面。兩者合在一起才構成可演出的資訊，舞台指示不能當成角色直接說出的內容。

sections.heading: 角色目標推動衝突
sections.body: 想搭末班車、想把錢用作禮物、想保存作為旅行基金，都是不同目標；當資源或時間不能同時滿足目標，就形成衝突。先寫每個角色要什麼，再看對話如何協商或改變。

sections.heading: 道具和動作可以成為線索
sections.body: 手機燈、保險絲開關、紅圍巾與遺失布條不只是背景物件，它們可能揭示問題、串聯角色或象徵互助。但解讀道具功能必須回到它出現、被使用與結局的前後關係。

sections.heading: 結局要回應前面的問題
sections.body: 短劇結尾若說 We solved it because we listened，便把解決方案和傾聽連起來；若角色從小聲道歉到主動解釋，代表可由前後行動支持的改變。不能只把最後一句當成獨立格言。

studyHighlights: 分開台詞、舞台指示、道具與燈光，再整合成可演出的情節。
用角色目標和資源／時間限制辨識衝突與協商。
追蹤道具、動作和線索在問題、轉折與結局中的功能。
以結尾回應開頭問題，並用前後台詞或動作證明人物改變與主旨。

body.heading: 方括號裡的動作也在說話嗎？
body.body: 給學生一段原創劇本：Mia points to the dark window and steps back。學生先只讀台詞猜場面，再加入舞台指示比較觀眾知道的危險、距離與情緒，理解非口語線索的戲劇功能。

body.heading: 短劇六格排演卡
body.body: 建立 Role、Goal、Stage clue、Conflict、Choice、Outcome 六格。先標角色想做什麼，再把舞台動作、對話與道具放入事件鏈，最後檢查結局是否回應衝突。

body.heading: 由燈光和道具找到解決方案
body.body: 以停電場景示範：lights go out 是問題，phone light 讓角色能看見，fuse switch 提供解決線索；不能把使用手機燈誤說成已修好電力。

body.heading: 台詞、動作與結局輪換
body.body: 用錢包、報告、末班車、班級禮物、紅圍巾與布條六組原創短劇，學生輪流回答角色目標、舞台指示、衝突、道具功能與結局主旨，並在劇本上圈出證據。每次先遮去一類資訊再重讀，觀察若拿掉走位、燈光或道具提示，觀眾會少知道什麼，最後用兩處不同線索確認結局是否回應原本衝突。

body.heading: 把閱讀答案變成排演提示
body.body: 學生將一場短劇改寫成三張演員提示卡：誰要什麼、哪個動作改變局面、結尾如何收束。每張卡附上對應台詞或舞台指示；交換後請同伴只依提示卡重述情節，檢查是否漏掉關鍵線索、誤把暫時方案當成問題已解決，或把尚未發生的事說成結局。

body.heading: 我忽略了哪一種舞台資訊？
body.body: 回看答案，標記把舞台指示當台詞、把道具當裝飾、把衝突當角色性格、把方案當結局或把最後一句脫離情節的錯誤。修訂時補回動作、目的與結果的連結，並追問角色的目標是否改變、障礙是否消失、道具是否真的產生預期作用；沒有文本證據的心理解讀要改成可能性。

summary: 分辨 Role、Goal、Stage clue、Conflict、Choice、Outcome 六種短劇資訊。
從台詞與舞台指示共同建立角色目標、問題與行動。
以道具、燈光和走位追蹤線索與解決方案。
用前後排演證據理解人物改變、結局與主旨。

exitCheck.prompt: 舞台指示和台詞如何共同傳達場景？
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能指出方括號動作或燈光提供的非口語資訊，並說明它如何補充角色台詞。

exitCheck.prompt: 如何判斷短劇中的主要衝突？
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能分別說出角色目標與阻礙，並指出哪段對話或動作顯示兩者碰撞。

exitCheck.prompt: 結局主旨為什麼要回看前面的排演線索？
exitCheck.expectedEvidence: 能用問題、選擇、道具或人物前後行動解釋結尾，而非只摘錄最後一句。

interactive.goal: 整合短劇台詞、舞台指示、角色目標、道具與結局，理解衝突、解決方案與人物改變。
interactive.scenario: 學生擔任小劇場導讀員，要為演員標出角色目標、舞台線索與能解決問題的關鍵行動。

shortPlayLab.label: 台詞 × 舞台指示 × 劇情
shortPlayLab.title: 讀懂一場排演如何解決衝突
shortPlayLab.goal: 先預測短劇問題，再把角色目標、舞台動作、道具功能、轉折和結局串成有證據的劇情理解，最後遷移到另一齣新戲。

preview.title: A Clear Path
preview.cue: 排演提示：一張空椅子、一輪紙月亮，以及地板上一條藍色膠帶線。先猜這些線索為什麼會同時出現在舞台上。

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Mina hangs a silver ribbon from the paper moon. It falls across the blue tape line.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The empty chair belongs under the moon in our final scene.

lines.speaker: Ivo
lines.text: The ribbon blocks the marked path. Sam cannot roll his chair through it.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: We have five minutes. Can the picture stay clear and the path stay open?

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Mina kneels beside the blue tape instead of lifting the ribbon.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The tape marks the clear route. Move the chair upstage; the audience can still see the moon.

lines.speaker: Ivo
lines.text: I will move the prop stand. Sam, please test the route.

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Sam rolls across the stage. His wheels pass the chair without touching the ribbon.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The route is clear, and the moon is still visible from my seat.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Then we have our final picture. Everyone takes a place beside the open path.

mainStages.prompt: What problem must the group solve before the final scene can work?
options: They must keep the paper moon but make sure the ribbon and chair do not block Sam's route.
They must find a new actor because Sam has left the theater.
They must replace the blue tape because the audience cannot see the moon.
mainStages.feedback: The group needs both a clear stage picture and an open route; the conflict is about meeting both needs.
mainStages.retryHint: Compare Mina's plan for the final picture with Ivo's warning about the route. What two needs seem to clash?

mainStages.prompt: Why does the stage direction show Mina kneeling beside the blue tape?
options: She checks the marked route for a clue before suggesting a change.
She is pretending to fall so the audience will laugh.
She is hiding the paper moon from the director.
mainStages.feedback: Her action directs attention to the tape as useful stage evidence, and her next line explains how it guides the solution.
mainStages.retryHint: Read the action and Mina's next spoken line together. Which object does she inspect, and what does she learn from it?

mainStages.prompt: How does the silver ribbon affect the scene before the group changes the layout?
options: It decorates the moon and also falls across the route, creating a practical obstacle.
It proves that the final scene takes place outdoors.
It tells Sam that he should leave the stage.
mainStages.feedback: The same prop contributes to the visual design but becomes part of the conflict when it crosses the taped route.
mainStages.retryHint: Track where the ribbon is attached and where it falls. Does it only decorate, or does its position change what Sam can do?

mainStages.prompt: Which event turns the argument into a workable plan?
options: The director says there are only five minutes left.
Mina uses the tape route to propose moving the chair, and Ivo asks Sam to test it.
Sam repeats that the ribbon is silver.
mainStages.feedback: Mina connects a visible clue to a new arrangement; Ivo then turns the proposal into a testable action.
mainStages.retryHint: Look for the moment when someone uses a stage clue to suggest a change, then notice who helps check that idea.

mainStages.prompt: Which statement best explains the ending using the group's actions?
options: A strong stage picture matters more than whether everyone can use the stage.
Listening to the people affected and testing a new arrangement can solve a shared design problem.
A silver ribbon always makes a play successful.
mainStages.feedback: The open route and visible moon are both confirmed by Sam's test, so the ending grows from listening and checking the solution.
mainStages.retryHint: Use Sam's final report and the director's decision. Which choice accounts for both the clear route and the visible moon?

mainStages.prompt: What change in Ivo's role can the audience infer from his lines and actions?
options: He moves from naming the obstacle to helping test a shared solution.
He refuses to take part after Mina explains the tape.
He changes the subject because the scene is over.
mainStages.feedback: Ivo first identifies the blocked route, then moves equipment and invites Sam to test the plan; his actions show practical cooperation.
mainStages.retryHint: Compare Ivo's warning about the blocked path with his later offer to move the stand. What does he do after the plan is proposed?

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Ari begins the opening line while Noor taps a hand drum beside the curtain.

lines.speaker: Ari
lines.text: The first words disappear when the drum starts. The back row cannot hear them.

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Noor stops tapping and looks toward the back row.

lines.speaker: Noor
lines.text: The drum can mark the entrance, but it does not need to cover the words.

lines.speaker: 舞台指示
lines.text: Noor raises one finger. Ari speaks the first line; the drum joins softly after the final word.

lines.speaker: Ari
lines.text: Now the back row can hear the line, and the drum still signals the scene.

stages.prompt: What is the opening scene's main problem?
options: The drum covers Ari's words, so the audience cannot hear the opening line.
Noor has forgotten how to play any instrument.
The actors cannot find the curtain.
stages.feedback: Ari states the sound problem and identifies who is affected: listeners in the back row.
stages.retryHint: Read Ari's line and note what the back row cannot hear. Keep the answer tied to that stated problem.

stages.prompt: What does Noor's raised finger do in the new arrangement?
options: It cues the drum to enter after Ari's line, instead of covering the words.
It signals Ari to leave before the scene begins.
It asks the audience to clap over the dialogue.
stages.feedback: The gesture is a stage cue; the next direction shows the order changing so speech comes first and music follows softly.
stages.retryHint: Follow the order after the finger rises: who speaks first, and when does the drum begin?

stages.prompt: Which idea best fits the result of this second play?
options: A performance works only when every sound is loud.
A cue should help the audience follow the scene; performers can adjust after noticing what listeners need.
The back row should guess words they cannot hear.
stages.feedback: The actors keep the drum's signaling role but change its timing and volume after considering the listeners' experience.
stages.retryHint: Compare the old sound order with the new one and use Ari's final line. What changed, and who benefited?
